literature.headline_zh: 诺如病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期诺如病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 在中心3周的污水系列中,GII.4具有最高的平均基于读数的相对丰度(31.1%),其次是GII.17(17.5%)和GII.7(15.2%)。在严格每周比较中,污水中GII.17的代表性低于零星病例(-32.6个百分点),污水中GII.7的代表性低于诺如病毒(-14.0个百分点)。 [10.1016/j.meegid.2026.106045]
突变分析表明,VP1位点373和392的氨基酸共同调控HBGA配体结合。血清学分析显示这些位点的抗原性影响较小。更广泛的GII比较揭示了胆汁影响的差异,胆汁增强了GII.2和GII.12对HBGA的结合,但对GII.4和GII.6则没有这种效果。 [10.1128/jvi.01338-26]
成功从粪便样本中回收了五株近完整的GII.4[P31]型诺如病毒病毒基因组基因组序列。 [10.1128/mra.00748-26]
检测到HAV RNA的样本占近6%(n = 10),而诺如病毒基因组I和II分别在1.2%(n = 2)和0.6%(n = 1)的样本中被发现。 [10.3390/v18101143]
在2018年的TAC检测样本中,检测到了10%的诺如病毒 GII.4。其他常见检测到的病原体包括腺病毒40/41(2017年28%,2018年3%)、肠聚集性大肠杆菌(EAEC)(27%和28%)以及诺如病毒 GII(11%和10%)。 [10.1186/s12887-026-07875-3]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: In the centred 3-week wastewater series, GII.4 had the highest mean read-based relative abundance (31.1%), followed by GII.17 (17.5%) and GII.7 (15.2%). [10.1016/j.meegid.2026.106045]

Mutational analysis demonstrated that amino acids at VP1 positions 373 and 392 coregulate HBGA ligand binding. Serological analysis showed minimal antigenic impact at these positions. Broader GII comparisons revealed variable impacts of bile, with bile improving GII.2 and GII.12 binding to HBGA but not GII.4 and GII.6. [10.1128/jvi.01338-26]
Five near-complete norovirus genomes of genotype GII.4[P31] were successfully recovered from the stool samples. [10.1128/mra.00748-26]
HAV RNA was detected in nearly 6% of samples (n = 10), while norovirus genogroup I and II were found in 1.2% (n = 2) and 0.6% (n = 1) of samples, respectively. [10.3390/v18101143]

news.headline_zh: 诺如病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期诺如病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 一项实地调查发现,中国一所大学存在 诺如病毒 GII.17 暴发,该病毒与食堂就餐有关,该研究的作者在《BMC 传染病》上进行了报道。 [news-add3aa9bdd7bb2e9]
疑似 诺如病毒 暴发 在从罗德岛飞往杜塞尔多夫的欧洲之翼航班上;3名乘客住院。 [news-1ce6d05844d40f24]

October 20, 2026/3 min read Airline British Airways Heathrow Baileys Slip Case: £4 Million Disability Dispute A judge has ordered British Airways to pay £100,000 in interim compensation to a businessman who claims a Baileys spill. [news-7ca2dedb755fc902]
文章报道称,诺如病毒 病例仍高于平均水平,英国卫生与安全局 (UKHSA) 指出,与 5 个季节的平均水平相比,2026 年第 35 周至第 38 周期间的实验室报告有所增加。 [news-1e5ae632cec855ff]
Western Isles Hospital报告了诺如病毒 暴发,导致2号内科病房关闭。暴发被证实首先影响外科病房,随后影响内科病房。目前,医院病房已重新开放收治病人。 [news-78e0a015fc060236]

news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Norovirus news developments.
key_findings_en: A field investigation identified a norovirus GII.17 outbreak at a Chinese university, associated with dining at the canteen, and reported by the study authors in BMC Infectious Diseases. [news-add3aa9bdd7bb2e9]
Suspected norovirus outbreak onboard a Eurowings flight from Rhodes to Düsseldorf; 3 passengers hospitalized. [news-1ce6d05844d40f24]

October 20, 2026/3 min read Airline British Airways Heathrow Baileys Slip Case: £4 Million Disability Dispute A judge has ordered British Airways to pay £100,000 in interim compensation to a businessman who claims a Baileys spill. [news-7ca2dedb755fc902]

The article reports that norovirus cases remain higher than average, with the UK Health and Security Agency (UKHSA) noting increased laboratory reports between weeks 35 and 38 of 2026 compared to the 5-season average. [news-1e5ae632cec855ff]

A norovirus outbreak was reported at Western Isles Hospital, leading to the closure of Medical Ward 2. The outbreak was confirmed to have affected the surgical ward first, and later the medical ward. The hospital ward has now reopened to admissions. [news-78e0a015fc060236]

papers.title: Near-complete genome sequences of five norovirus GII.4[P31] strains from coastal Kenya, 2019
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT There is limited norovirus genomic data from Africa. We report five near-complete norovirus genomes of genotype GII.4[P31], recovered from stool samples of children admitted with acute diarrhea in coastal Kenya during 2019. These expand the available genomic data resource for norovirus evolutionary studies, molecular assay improvement, and therapeutics development.

We report five near-complete norovirus genomes of genotype GII.4[P31], recovered from stool samples of children admitted with acute diarrhea in coastal Kenya during 2019. These expand the available genomic data resource for norovirus evolutionary studies, molecular assay improvement, and therapeutics development.

papers.title_original: Near-complete genome sequences of five norovirus GII.4[P31] strains from coastal Kenya, 2019

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of genomic data on norovirus in Africa, which is critical for understanding its epidemiology and evolution in the region.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the recovery of five near-complete norovirus genomes from stool samples of children with acute diarrhea in coastal Kenya during 2019.
analysis.methods: The researchers sequenced the genomes to expand the genomic data resource for norovirus evolutionary studies, molecular assay improvement, and therapeutics development.
analysis.main_results: Five near-complete norovirus genomes of genotype GII.4[P31] were successfully recovered from the stool samples.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings provide new genomic data for norovirus in Africa, contributing to the understanding of its genetic diversity and evolution in the region.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The data can inform surveillance efforts and improve molecular assays for norovirus detection in Africa, which is essential for public health preparedness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a small number of samples and does not provide detailed epidemiological or clinical data, but the evidence is strong due to the direct sequencing of the viral genomes.

analysis.summary_en: This study reports the sequencing of five near-complete norovirus GII.4[P31] genomes from children with acute diarrhea in coastal Kenya during 2019. The research was motivated by the limited genomic data on norovirus in Africa, which hampers understanding of its epidemiology and evolution. The study expands the genomic resource for norovirus, offering insights into genetic diversity and potential for molecular assay improvement. The findings are significant for surveillance and public health in the region, though the small sample size limits broader generalizability. The evidence is strong due to the direct sequencing of the viral genomes, which provides reliable data for further research.

papers.title: Genotype-resolved wastewater surveillance for monitoring human norovirus GII circulation
papers.abstract: Norovirus GII causes a substantial global burden of acute gastroenteritis, and genotype-resolved wastewater surveillance offers a complementary approach for monitoring community circulation beyond cases captured by routine clinical surveillance. We monitored four municipal wastewater treatment plants in Beijing, China, from October 2023 to September 2024 and compared weekly GII genotype profiles with contemporaneous sporadic-case and outbreak surveillance. Strict-weekly genotype comparisons were the primary inference and used moving-block bootstrap confidence intervals, block-sign tests, and false-discovery-rate correction; centred 3-week profiles were used for description and sensitivity analysis. Bray-Curtis dissimilarity quantified compositional concordance, and same-week and lagged Spearman correlations compared wastewater GII concentration with clinical surveillance activity. In the centred 3-week wastewater series, GII.4 had the highest mean read-based relative abundance (31.1%), followed by GII.17 (17.5%) and GII.7 (15.2%). In strict-weekly comparisons, wastewater had lower GII.17 representation than sporadic cases (-32.6 percentage points) and lower GII.7 representation than outbreaks (-14.0 percentage points). Wastewater had higher GII.3, GII.4, GII.6, and GII.9 representation than sporadic cases and higher GII.9 and GII.13 representation than outbreaks; the GII.4 and GII.7 differences were sensitive to analytical specification, and the GII.13 effect was small. Mean strict-weekly Bray-Curtis dissimilarities were 0.590-0.679 in 32 common weeks. Same-week and lagged wastewater concentration correlations with sporadic-case positivity and outbreak case counts were not significant after temporal-dependence and multiplicity correction. Genotype-resolved wastewater surveillance documented co-circulating GII genotypes and recurrent source-specific differences, while read-based relative abundance remained dependent on catchment coverage and genotype-specific analytical performance.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to monitor the circulation of human norovirus GII genotypes using genotype-resolved wastewater surveillance, complementing routine clinical data. Four wastewater treatment plants in Beijing were monitored from October 2023 to September 2024, with weekly GII genotype profiles compared to sporadic-case and outbreak surveillance. The methods involved strict-weekly comparisons using statistical techniques like moving-block bootstrap confidence intervals and false-discovery-rate correction, alongside centred 3-week profiles for sensitivity analysis. The main results showed that GII.4 had the highest mean read-based relative abundance in wastewater, followed by GII.17 and GII.7. In strict-weekly comparisons, wastewater had lower GII.17 and GII.7 representation than sporadic cases and outbreaks, respectively. The authors interpreted these findings as evidence of co-circulating GII genotypes and source-specific differences, highlighting the utility of wastewater surveillance for tracking norovirus circulation. The study's significance lies in its potential to improve surveillance strategies for norovirus, while its limitations include non-significant correlations between wastewater concentrations and clinical data after statistical corrections.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 诺如病毒GII导致了全球范围内的急性胃肠炎重大负担,而基于基因型的污水监测提供了一种补充方法,用于监测社区传播情况,超越了常规临床监测所捕捉的病例。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们在中国北京监测了四个市政污水诺如病毒处理厂,时间从2023年10月至2024年9月,并将每周的GII基因型谱与同期的零星病例和诺如病毒监测数据进行比较。
elements_zh.methods: 严格的每周基因型比较是主要推断方法,使用移动块自举置信区间、块符号检验和错误发现率校正;以中心3周的谱型用于描述和敏感性分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 在中心3周的污水系列中,GII.4具有最高的平均基于读数的相对丰度(31.1%),其次是GII.17(17.5%)和GII.7(15.2%)。在严格每周比较中,污水中GII.17的代表性低于零星病例(-32.6个百分点),污水中GII.7的代表性低于诺如病毒(-14.0个百分点)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 基于基因型的污水监测记录了共循环的GII基因型和反复出现的来源特异性差异,而基于读数的相对丰度仍依赖于排水区域覆盖范围和基因型特异性分析性能。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 基于基因型的污水监测可用于指导诺如病毒监测策略,以追踪人类诺如病毒GII的流行情况,并检测可能影响公共卫生应对的基因型变化。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 在32个共同周中,严格每周的Bray-Curtis差异度平均为0.590-0.679。在时间依赖性和多重性校正后,污水浓度与零星病例阳性率和诺如病毒病例数的同期和滞后相关性均不显著。

papers.title: Systematic functional, genomic, and safety evaluation of food-derived anti-human norovirus candidate Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus YQ001
papers.abstract: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus YQ001 is a yogurt-derived strain previously reported to bind GII.4 human norovirus (HuNoV) and inhibit viral replication in zebrafish larvae. Here, its in vitro probiotic properties and preliminary safety were evaluated together with whole-genome analysis. The 2.87-Mb genome (46.67% GC; 2757 coding sequences) shared 97.66% average nucleotide identity with L. rhamnosus GG ATCC 53103. L. rhamnosus YQ001 showed acid and bile tolerance, retaining approximately 30% survival after 3 h at pH 2.0 and over 40% after 4 h in 0.2% bile salts. During sequential simulated gastrointestinal digestion, L. rhamnosus YQ001 retained 35.98% survival after the gastric phase and 45.06% after the intestinal phase. L. rhamnosus YQ001 showed over 90% auto-aggregation at 24 h, while its cell-free supernatant exhibited DPPH and ABTS radical-scavenging activities of 85.17% and 76.35%, respectively. Antibacterial activity detected by agar diffusion was abolished after pH neutralization, indicating that the observed inhibition was largely pH-dependent under the tested conditions. L. rhamnosus YQ001 was non-hemolytic and negative for gelatinase and nitroreductase activities. Overall, the phenotypic and genomic findings support the probiotic potential of L. rhamnosus YQ001, while further strain-specific functional and safety evaluation is warranted.

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为乳酸乳球菌YZQ001作为诺如病毒感染的益生菌候选菌株的使用提供了初步支持,可能对未来该领域的研究和开发提供参考。

papers.abstract_zh: 乳酸乳球菌YZQ001是一种从酸奶中分离的菌株,此前报道可结合GII.4人类诺如病毒(HuNoV)并在斑马鱼幼鱼中抑制病毒复制。本研究对其体外益生菌特性及初步安全性进行了评估,并进行了全基因组分析。该菌株的全基因组为2.87 Mb(GC含量46.67%;包含2757个编码序列),与乳酸乳球菌GG ATCC 53103的平均核苷酸同源性为97.66%。乳酸乳球菌YZQ001表现出酸和胆盐耐受性,在pH 2.0条件下3小时后存活率约为30%,在0.2%胆盐中4小时后存活率超过40%。在连续模拟胃肠消化过程中,乳酸乳球菌YZQ001在胃部消化阶段后存活率为35.98%,在肠道消化阶段后存活率为45.06%。该菌株在24小时后表现出超过90%的自聚集能力,其无细胞培养上清液表现出85.17%的DPPH自由基清除能力和76.35%的ABTS自由基清除能力。通过琼脂扩散法检测到的抗菌活性在pH中和后被消除,表明在测试条件下观察到的抑制作用主要依赖于pH值。乳酸乳球菌YZQ001不溶血,且不表现出明胶酶和硝基还原酶活性。总体而言,表型和基因组研究结果支持乳酸乳球菌YZQ001作为益生菌的潜力,但需要进一步进行菌株特异性功能和安全性评估。

papers.title: Bile and capsid variation coregulate histo-blood group antigen recognition and serum neutralization potency in GII.12 human norovirus
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Human norovirus (HuNoV) is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis, with young children and the elderly bearing the greatest disease burden. GII strains cause the majority of HuNoV outbreaks globally, with host susceptibility influenced by genetic polymorphisms that regulate mucosal expression of histo-blood group antigen (HBGA) binding ligands. HuNoV viral capsid (VP1) diversity in residues adjacent to the conserved HBGA binding pocket selectively stabilizes ligand interactions. Additionally, select HuNoV capsids demonstrate bile-influenced conformational plasticity, further enabling HBGA engagement. Combined, these factors have the potential to enhance the breadth of binding of HuNoV to HBGAs, driving population susceptibility. Here we characterized two GII.12 outbreak strains that co-circulated cotemporaneously and were divergent at five key VP1 sites. Mutational analysis demonstrated amino acids at VP1 positions 373 and 392 coregulate HBGA ligand binding. Serological analysis demonstrated minimal antigenic impact at these positions. Broader GII comparisons demonstrated variable impacts of bile. Bile improved GII.2 and GII.12 binding to HBGA, in contrast to GII.4, GII.3, and GII.6. Further, bile reduced surrogate neutralizing antibody potency for GII.2 and GII.12 but not GII.4 and GII.6 strains. Collectively, these studies suggest that HuNoV bile-dependence is not a general feature of GII norovirus, but instead can be genotype or strain specific. These data inform how select GII HuNoV strains can modulate capsid residues linked to host-ligand and immune recognition, providing potential mechanistic evidence for continual viral circulation. IMPORTANCE Human norovirus-host interactions are complex, influenced by viral diversity, host-ligand expression profiles, and the gastrointestinal environment. Periodically, outbreaks of endemic human noroviruses, like GII.12, demonstrate genetic diversity between viral strains of a genotype. Exploring this, two GII.12 outbreak strains were used to model the effects of genetic changes on the viral capsid ligand and antibody binding. Residue changes between the two strains modulated affinity for histo-blood group antigens that could be compensated for by addition of bile. Although bile improved HBGA-binding, it reduced serum and monoclonal antibody neutralization potency to GII.12. These observations demonstrate the balanced impact of bile-mediated viral capsid conformational plasticity in ligand recognition and potential immune evasion for select GII genotypes. Bile had similar effects for GII.2 HuNoV, but did not impact GII.6 or GII.4 HuNoV HBGA-binding and serum-ligand blocking potency, indicating that GII HuNoV strains potentially utilize multiple mechanisms to ensure host breadth and antigenic diversity.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human norovirus (HuNoV) is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis, with young children and the elderly bearing the greatest disease burden. The study aimed to understand how capsid variation and bile influence histo-blood group antigen (HBGA) recognition and serum neutralization potency in GII.12 HuNoV.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study characterized two GII.12 outbreak strains that co-circulated cotemporaneously and were divergent at five key VP1 sites. These strains were used to model the effects of genetic changes on viral capsid ligand and antibody binding. The research focused on GII.12 HuNoV strains and their interactions with host ligands and immune responses.
analysis.methods: Mutational analysis was used to assess the impact of amino acid changes at VP1 positions 373 and 392 on HBGA ligand binding. Serological analysis evaluated the antigenic impact of these changes. Broader GII comparisons assessed the variable effects of bile on HBGA-binding and neutralizing antibody potency.
analysis.main_results: Mutational analysis demonstrated that amino acids at VP1 positions 373 and 392 coregulate HBGA ligand binding. Serological analysis showed minimal antigenic impact at these positions. Broader GII comparisons revealed variable impacts of bile, with bile improving GII.2 and GII.12 binding to HBGA but not GII.4 and GII.6.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that bile-mediated conformational plasticity of the viral capsid can modulate ligand recognition and immune evasion for select GII genotypes. This study provides potential mechanistic evidence for the continual circulation of GII.12 HuNoV strains.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These data inform the understanding of how specific GII HuNoV strains can modulate capsid residues linked to host-ligand and immune recognition, which may have implications for surveillance, diagnosis, and vaccine development targeting GII.12 strains.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on two GII.12 strains, which may not represent the full genetic diversity of GII.12 HuNoV. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on mutational and serological analyses of a limited set of strains.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how capsid variation and bile influence histo-blood group antigen (HBGA) recognition and serum neutralization potency in GII.12 human norovirus (HuNoV). The research highlights that amino acids at VP1 positions 373 and 392 coregulate HBGA binding, and that bile can enhance HBGA engagement but reduce neutralizing antibody potency for GII.12 strains. These findings suggest that bile-mediated conformational changes in the viral capsid may contribute to immune evasion and the continued circulation of GII.12 HuNoV. papers.title_zh: 胆汁和衣壳变异共同调控组胺血型抗原识别和血清中和能力在GII.12人类诺如病毒中
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Human norovirus (HuNoV) is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis, with young children and the elderly bearing the greatest disease burden. GII strains cause the majority of HuNoV outbreaks globally, with host susceptibility influenced by genetic polymorphisms that regulate mucosal expression of histo-blood group antigen (HBGA) binding ligands. HuNoV viral capsid (VP1) diversity in residues adjacent to the conserved HBGA binding pocket selectively stabilizes ligand interactions. Additionally, select HuNoV capsids demonstrate bile-influenced conformational plasticity, further enabling HBGA engagement. Combined, these factors have the potential to enhance the breadth of binding of HuNoV to HBGAs, driving population susceptibility. Here we characterized two GII.12 outbreak strains that co-circulated cotemporaneously and were divergent at five key VP1 sites. Mutational analysis demonstrated amino acids at VP1 positions 373 and 392 coregulate HBGA ligand binding. Serological analysis demonstrated minimal antigenic impact at these positions. Broader GII comparisons demonstrated variable impacts of bile. Bile improved GII.2 and GII.12 binding to HBGA, in contrast to GII.4, GII.3, and GII.6. Further, bile reduced surrogate neutralizing antibody potency for GII.2 and GII.12 but not GII.4 and GII.6 strains. Collectively, these studies suggest that HuNoV bile-dependence is not a general feature of GII norovirus, but instead can be genotype or strain specific. These data inform how select GII HuNoV strains can modulate capsid residues linked to host-ligand and immune recognition, providing potential mechanistic evidence for continual viral circulation. IMPORTANCE Human norovirus-host interactions are complex, influenced by viral diversity, host-ligand expression profiles, and the gastrointestinal environment. Periodically, outbreaks of endemic human noroviruses, like GII.12, demonstrate genetic diversity between viral strains of a genotype. Exploring this, two GII.12 outbreak strains were used to model the effects of genetic changes on the viral capsid ligand and antibody binding. Residue changes between the two strains modulated affinity for histo-blood group antigens that could be compensated for by addition of bile. Although bile improved HBGA-binding, it reduced serum and monoclonal antibody neutralization potency to GII.12. These observations demonstrate the balanced impact of bile-mediated viral capsid conformational plasticity in ligand recognition and potential immune evasion for select GII genotypes. Bile had similar effects for GII.2 HuNoV, but did not impact GII.6 or GII.4 HuNoV HBGA-binding and serum-ligand blocking potency, indicating that GII HuNoV strains potentially utilize multiple mechanisms to ensure host breadth and antigenic diversity.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 人类诺如病毒(HuNoV)是急性胃肠炎的主要病因之一,年轻儿童和老年人承担着最大的疾病负担。GII型株在全球范围内导致了大多数HuNoV感染,其易感性受到调控黏膜表达组胺血型抗原(HBGA)结合配体的遗传多态性的影响。HuNoV病毒衣壳(VP1)在保守的HBGA结合位点附近的残基多样性可选择性稳定配体相互作用。此外,某些HuNoV衣壳表现出胆汁影响的构象可塑性,进一步促进HBGA的结合。综上所述,这些因素可能增强HuNoV对HBGA的结合范围,从而驱动人群易感性。在这里,我们表征了两种同时共循环的GII.12 暴发株,它们在五个关键VP1位点上存在差异。突变分析表明,VP1位点373和392的氨基酸共同调控HBGA配体结合。血清学分析表明,这些位点的抗原性影响较小。更广泛的GII比较显示胆汁对HBGA结合的影响存在差异。胆汁增强了GII.2和GII.12对HBGA的结合,但对GII.4、GII.3和GII.6则没有这种效果。此外,胆汁降低了GII.2和GII.12的替代中和抗体效力,但对GII.4和GII.6株则没有影响。总体而言,这些研究结果表明,HuNoV对胆汁的依赖性并不是GII 诺如病毒的普遍特征,而是可能与基因型或菌株特异性相关。这些数据有助于理解某些GII HuNoV菌株如何调节与组胺血型抗原配体和免疫识别相关的衣壳残基,为病毒持续传播提供了潜在的机制证据。重要性 人类诺如病毒与组胺血型抗原的相互作用是复杂的,受到病毒多样性、组胺血型抗原配体表达谱以及胃肠道环境的影响。有时,流行性人类诺如病毒,如GII.12,其病毒株之间会表现出基因型内的遗传多样性。本研究通过使用两种GII.12 暴发菌株来模拟遗传变化对病毒衣壳配体和抗体结合的影响。两种菌株之间的残基变化调节了对组胺血型抗原的亲和力,这种亲和力可以通过添加胆汁得到补偿。尽管胆汁增强了HBGA结合,但它却降低了对GII.12的血清和单克隆抗体中和能力。这些观察结果表明,胆汁介导的病毒衣壳构象可塑性对配体识别和某些GII基因型的潜在免疫逃逸具有平衡影响。对于GII.2 HuNoV,胆汁具有类似的效果,但对GII.6或GII.4 HuNoV的HBGA结合和血清-配体阻断能力没有影响,这表明GII HuNoV菌株可能利用多种机制来确保对组胺血型抗原的广泛结合和抗原多样性。

papers.title: Occurrence of Norovirus and Hepatitis A Virus RNA in Agricultural Soil from Produce Farms in Ohio and Georgia
papers.abstract: Although foodborne viruses are considered ubiquitous in the environment, studies on their presence in soil are largely lacking. In this field study, 168 agricultural soil samples were collected from farms in Georgia and Ohio over seven and eight months, respectively. A total RNA isolation method was developed, and extracted genetic material was analyzed using reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) to detect human norovirus and hepatitis A virus (HAV) RNA. Nearly 6% of samples (n = 10) tested positive for HAV RNA, while norovirus genogroup I and II were detected in 1.2% (n = 2) and 0.6% (n = 1) of samples, respectively. Despite samples being stored at −20 °C for an average of two years prior to testing, viruses remained detectable, although in low levels. CrAssphage DNA and pepper mild mottle virus (PMMoV) RNA were assessed as indicators of human fecal contamination in positive samples; however, neither was detected, precluding any correlation with the viral pathogens—likely due to differing characteristics between the indicators and target viruses. These findings provide valuable insight into the prevalence and diversity of foodborne viruses in agricultural soil and highlight its potential as a vehicle for virus transport to other matrices within a fresh produce farm environment.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the occurrence of norovirus and hepatitis A virus RNA in agricultural soil, addressing the lack of research on foodborne viruses in such environments.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A field study was conducted over seven and eight months in Ohio and Georgia, respectively, collecting 168 agricultural soil samples from produce farms.
analysis.methods: Total RNA was isolated from soil samples, and reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) was used to detect human norovirus and hepatitis A virus (HAV) RNA.
analysis.main_results: HAV RNA was detected in nearly 6% of samples (n = 10), while norovirus genogroup I and II were found in 1.2% (n = 2) and 0.6% (n = 1) of samples, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors suggest that the presence of these viruses in soil indicates a potential role in virus transport within fresh produce farm environments, highlighting the need for further investigation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the importance of monitoring agricultural soil for foodborne viruses to better understand their role in contaminating fresh produce and contributing to public health risks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is limited by the potential for false negatives due to the storage conditions of the samples, and the results are based on a single testing method, which may not capture all viral variants.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the presence of norovirus and hepatitis A virus RNA in agricultural soil from produce farms in Ohio and Georgia. Soil samples were collected over seven and eight months, respectively, and total RNA was isolated and analyzed using RT-qPCR. The results showed that HAV RNA was detected in nearly 6% of samples, while norovirus genogroup I and II were found in 1.2% and 0.6% of samples, respectively. The authors suggest that these findings highlight the potential of agricultural soil as a vehicle for virus transport within farm environments. However, the study's evidence is limited by the storage conditions of the samples and the use of a single testing method, which may affect the reliability of the results. The findings provide valuable insight into the prevalence of foodborne viruses in soil and their implications for public health.

papers.title_zh: Ohio和Georgia地区农产品农场土壤中诺如病毒和戊型肝炎病毒RNA的分布
papers.source_body_en: Although foodborne viruses are considered ubiquitous in the environment, studies on their presence in soil are largely lacking. In this field study, 168 agricultural soil samples were collected from farms in Georgia and Ohio over seven and eight months, respectively. A total RNA isolation method was developed, and extracted genetic material was analyzed using reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) to detect human norovirus and hepatitis A virus (HAV) RNA. Nearly 6% of samples (n = 10) tested positive for HAV RNA, while norovirus genogroup I and II were detected in 1.2% (n = 2) and 0.6% (n = 1) of samples, respectively. Despite samples being stored at −20 °C for an average of two years prior to testing, viruses remained detectable, although in low levels. CrAssphage DNA and pepper mild mottle virus (PMMoV) RNA were assessed as indicators of human fecal contamination in positive samples; however, neither was detected, precluding any correlation with the viral pathogens—likely due to differing characteristics between the indicators and target viruses. These findings provide valuable insight into the prevalence and diversity of foodborne viruses in agricultural soil and highlight its potential as a vehicle for virus transport to other matrices within a fresh produce farm environment.
papers.abstract_zh: 尽管食源性病毒被认为普遍存在于环境中,但针对其在土壤中分布情况的研究仍较为缺乏。在这项实地研究中,分别历时7个月和8个月,从佐治亚州和俄亥俄州的农场采集了168份农业土壤样本。研究人员建立了一种总RNA分离方法,并采用逆转录定量PCR(RT-qPCR)分析提取的遗传物质,以检测人诺如病毒和甲型肝炎病毒(HAV)RNA。近6%的样本(n = 10)HAV RNA检测呈阳性,而样本中诺如病毒基因组I和II的检出率分别为1.2%(n = 2)和0.6%(n = 1)。尽管样本在检测前平均于−20 °C条件下储存了2年,病毒仍可检出,但检出水平较低。研究在阳性样本中评估了CrAssphage DNA和辣椒轻斑驳病毒(PMMoV)RNA作为人粪便污染指标的情况;然而,两者均未检出,因此无法与病毒性病原体进行相关性分析,这可能是由于指标物与目标病毒的特性不同所致。这些发现为深入了解患病率以及食源性病毒的多样性提供了宝贵认识,并凸显了其在新鲜农产品农场环境中作为病毒向其他基质转移媒介的潜在作用。

papers.full_text: Abstract Background Norovirus (NoV) is a major pathogen responsible for acute gastroenteritis and outbreaks of diarrhea in humans. Children, due to their underdeveloped immune systems and higher risk of exposure, constitute a population with a relatively concentrated incidence of infection and disease burden. In recent years, research on NoV infections in children has been growing globally; however, there remains a lack of systematic quantitative analysis regarding the evolution of research themes, models of international collaboration, and future development directions in this field. Therefore, this study employs bibliometric methods to conduct a visual analysis of the knowledge structure, research hotspots, and development trends in the global field of NoV infection research in children, providing a reference for future scientific research and the formulation of prevention and control strategies. Methods This study retrieved literature on pediatric NoV infections published between January 1998 and December 2025 from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) database. Using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and Bibliometrix software, we conducted a visual analysis of annual publication trends, countries/regions, institutions, authors, journals, keywords, and references to reveal the research trajectory, knowledge base, and cutting-edge directions in this field. Results This study included a total of 2,161 relevant publications. The results show that research on NoV infections in children worldwide has generally followed a steady upward trend, with activity remaining high in recent years. The United States, China, and Japan are the leading contributors to research in this field, with the United States exerting significant influence through international collaboration. The University of Tokyo, Emory University, and Chiang Mai University are the research institutions with the highest number of publications. Vinje, Jan; Ushijima, Hiroshi; and Khamrin, Pattara were the most prolific core authors, while Atmar, Robert L.; Lindesmith, Lisa C.; and Patel, Manish M. demonstrated strong academic influence. Keyword analysis revealed that research in this field primarily focuses on viral molecular characteristics, epidemiological features, and clinical manifestations in children, and is gradually expanding toward disease burden assessment, global prevention and control strategies, and vaccine development. Conclusion Global research on NoV infections in children has evolved into a Multi-Disciplinary research framework driven by virology, epidemiology, clinical medicine, and public health. Current research focuses primarily on molecular epidemiology and genetic diversity, as well as epidemiological characteristics and outbreak transmission mechanisms, while the assessment of disease burden and the optimization of global prevention and control strategies are gradually emerging as key future research directions. In the future, international collaboration, multicenter surveillance, and interdisciplinary research should be further strengthened to advance research on pediatric NoV infection from describing disease characteristics toward precision surveillance, proactive prevention, and comprehensive control and prevention measures. Introduction Norovirus (NoV) is one of the primary pathogens causing acute gastroenteritis and outbreaks of diarrhea in humans. It is highly contagious and spreads rapidly, is prevalent worldwide, and is considered the fifth leading cause of disability-adjusted life years in the global disease burden [1]. The general population is widely susceptible to NoV, with over 700 million cases of infection and 200,000 deaths reported annually. Children under 5 years of age have the highest incidence rate, and this age group also has the highest diarrhea-related mortality rate [2, 3]. NoV is primarily transmitted via the fecal–oral route, accounting for 63.20% of foodborne viral infections. It can spread rapidly through contaminated shellfish, fruits, vegetables, ready-to-eat foods, and water sources, and is prone to causing cluster outbreaks in areas with poor sanitation in developing countries. Currently, there are no specific antiviral drugs or vaccines available [4]. In recent years, the number of NoV infections and outbreaks worldwide has continued to rise, causing serious impacts on human health and economic development [5]. Research findings on NoV infections in children continue to expand, with studies characterized by significant differences in research directions, scattered evidence, and intersecting disciplinary contexts. Traditional narrative reviews rely heavily on individual researchers’ literature screening and subjective interpretations, making it difficult to objectively quantify changes in publication timing within the field, connections among international research collaborations, and the evolution of knowledge. Meta-analyses can only conduct pooled effect analyses on a specific type of homogeneous clinical trial data to address specific scientific questions; they cannot trace shifts in research hotspots from a holistic perspective or identify seminal foundational literature and emerging research directions. In contrast, bibliometrics, drawing on mathematical statistics, information metrics, and visualization algorithms, enables unbiased quantitative analysis of large-scale literature datasets. It intuitively presents macro-level information such as annual output patterns, transnational collaboration networks, core research platforms, and the evolution of thematic clusters, thereby accurately identifying developmental blind spots and future frontier directions in the field [6]. Given the current heavy global burden of NoV infection among children and the persistent challenges in prevention and control, there is an urgent need to systematically map out the complete knowledge landscape of this field from a macro-level. Therefore, introducing bibliometric methods to conduct a panoramic quantitative analysis holds significant theoretical reference value and practical guidance. Through our preliminary search of major global academic databases, we found that there is still a gap in bibliometric research on NoV infection in children. Based on this, this study compiled basic information on global research related to NoV infection in children from 1998 to 2025. By using Citespace, VOSviewer, and Bibliometrix software to construct knowledge maps of the papers, the study aims to explore the current state of global research in this field, identify research hotspots, and outline future trends, thereby providing valuable direction and reference for future scientific exploration. Materials and methods Data sources and search strategies Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) is a Multi-Disciplinary citation index database developed by Clarivate Analytics. It includes more than 20,000 authoritative journals that have undergone rigorous peer review, covering over 250 disciplines. It features comprehensive metadata on authors, institutions, keywords, and references, preserves complete citation links, and allows for the direct batch export of standardized data compatible with bibliometric software. It is widely recognized as the most authoritative benchmark data source for constructing knowledge graphs [7, 8]. Although PubMed has advantages in biomedical retrieval, it lacks a complete structured citation index and cannot support core network analyses such as co-citation and literature coupling; Scopus has lower journal inclusion thresholds, incomplete retroactive citation tracking for early publications, and poor compatibility of its metadata format with mainstream bibliometric tools, which can easily introduce manual correction biases; Google Scholar contains a large amount of low-quality gray literature, resulting in distorted citation counts, and lacks standardized batch export functionality, making it difficult to meet the requirements for quantitative graph analysis [9, 10]. Therefore, this study selected WoSCC as the sole data source to ensure the accuracy and authority of the analysis results. On 1 April 2026, we searched the WoSCC (SCI-Expanded) database using the following search formula: TS = ((“Norovirus” OR “Norwalk virus” OR “Human noroviruses”) AND (“children” OR “infantile” OR “child” OR ‘childhood’ OR “pediatric”)). The search date range was set from 1 January 1998 to 31 December 2025; only articles and reviews were retained, and the language was restricted to “English”. Two researchers conducted the search and extracted data simultaneously and independently, with a third researcher performing the final verification to avoid selective bias. After collation, a total of 2,161 articles were ultimately included; all publications were exported as.txt files in “full record and reference list” format. The detailed search process is shown in Fig. 1. Bibliometric analysis CiteSpace is a bibliometric and scientific knowledge graph visualization tool developed by Professor Chen Chaomei’s team at Drexel University in the United States. It runs on Java and integrates citation analysis, complex network algorithms, temporal change detection, and information visualization technologies [11]. It is specifically designed to uncover the underlying patterns of association and evolutionary trajectories within long-term bibliographic datasets. We used CiteSpace (6.4.R1 Advanced) to visualize journal emergence, keyword clustering, keyword emergence, and reference emergence. Parameter settings: The “Time Slicing” range was set to 1998–2025, “Years Per Slice” was set to “1”, and “Node Types” were selected as “Journals”, “Keywords”, and “References”, respectively. For “Selection Criteria”, the default “g-index” (coefficient K = 25) was used. VOSviewer is a free, open-source bibliometric visualization tool developed by the Center for Science and Technology Studies at Leiden University in the Netherlands. It offers three interactive visualization modes: network view, overlay view, and density view [12]. We used VOSviewer (version 1.6.20) to analyze network patterns across countries, institutions, journals, authors, keywords, and references. For 'Type of analysis', 'Co-authorship' was selected for authors, institutions, and countries, while 'Co-occurrence' was selected for keywords and references. The 'Counting method' was set to 'Full counting', and the minimum item threshold was set to 2 occurrences. Display parameters and 'Labels' sizes were adjusted to reduce overlap and improve readability. Finally, 'Overlay Visualization' and 'Density Visualization' were selected for visual analysis. Bibliometrix is a comprehensive scientific mapping analysis system based on the R language that covers data import, cleaning, quantitative statistics, network analysis, and chart output [13]. In this study, we used it to visualize country collaborations and keyword frequencies. Prior to network analysis, country/region names were standardized using a predefined thesaurus. Three sovereign states—China, the United Kingdom, and the USA—had multiple alternative labels in the WoSCC export (including constituent countries, special administrative regions, and overseas territories); all such variants were merged under a single standardized label for each state. This merging rule was applied consistently across the dataset. A complete mapping of all original WoSCC country/region strings to standardized labels is provided in Supplementary File S1. Quality control Quality control was conducted in accordance with the preliminary BIBLIO guidelines [14], with six methodological items explicitly operationalized: data sources (Item 6), search strategy (Item 7), eligibility criteria (Item 9), data refinement (Item 10), quality assessment (Item 11), and data synthesis (Item 12). During literature retrieval and eligibility screening, two reviewers independently assessed all records, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer; inter-rater reliability was excellent (Cohen's κ = 0.92), as further detailed in Sect. "Data sources and search strategies". Country/region entity standardization and all software parameter thresholds were predefined prior to analysis, as described in Sect. "Bibliometric analysis". To support reproducibility, three supplementary files are provided: the per-record screening log (Supplementary File S2), the complete country/region thesaurus (Supplementary File S1), and a completed BIBLIO checklist mapping all 20 items to their corresponding locations in the manuscript (Supplementary File S3). These quality-control measures were applied uniformly throughout the study to mitigate selection bias and ensure methodological transparency. Results Trends in the number of publications Overall, the annual number of publications in this field has shown a clear upward trend over the past 28 years, although the rate of growth has varied somewhat across different periods (Fig. 2). From 1998 to 2004, the field was in its early stages, with an overall low annual output that fluctuated slightly, increasing from 6 papers in 1998 to 24 in 2004. From 2005 to 2013, research entered a phase of steady growth, with annual output gradually rising from 33 to 83 papers, indicating that NoV infection in children was gradually attracting more attention from researchers. From 2014 to 2025, research activity in this field increased significantly, with the annual number of publications exceeding 100 for the first time, reaching 122. It has since remained at a relatively high level overall, peaking at 150 in 2021—the highest figure during the study period. Between 2022 and 2025, the annual number of publications fluctuated somewhat but remained above 100. At the same time, the overall trend in annual citations generally followed the trend in publication volume, with citations exceeding 5,000 in each of the past five years. Overall, annual publications increased from 6 in 1998 to a peak of 150 in 2021, and annual citations exceeded 5,000 in each of the past five years, reflecting a sustained upward trend in research output and attention over the study period. Analysis of countries/regions and institutions A total of 130 countries/regions and 2,882 research institutions worldwide participated in studies related to NoV infection in children. The top three countries/regions in terms of publication volume were, in order, the USA (406 papers), CHINA (307 papers), and JAPAN (193 papers); together, these three contributed more than 40% of the research output and represent the most significant sources of research in this field (Table 1). The composition of single-country and multinational collaborative publications is shown in Fig. 3A. A comparison of MCP values reveals that the USA not only leads in total publications but also ranks first globally in the number of multinational collaborative publications; Japan has a relatively high proportion of international collaborative publications; and China, although second in total publications, has a relatively low proportion of multinational collaborative publications. In Fig. 3B, the lines connecting nodes represent co-authorship relationships between two countries/regions in the same publication; line thickness is positively correlated with collaboration frequency. The USA exhibits dense co-authorship links with multiple countries in Europe, Oceania, South America, and Asia, demonstrating the widest scope of collaboration; China and Japan also have multiple co-authorship links with neighboring Asian countries as well as European and American nations, indicating a high level of Participation. The overall network exhibits a cross-regional interconnected structure, with no completely isolated national nodes; direct or indirect co-occurrence collaboration links exist among the three major research regions of North America, East Asia, and Europe. The USA, Australia, and Germany rank among the top in terms of citations per paper, indicating that their research findings receive greater overall attention (Table 1). The top three institutions by publication volume are The University of Tokyo (84 papers), Emory University (66 papers), and Chiang Mai University (62 papers). The remaining high-output institutions are primarily U.S. universities and specialized research institutes, with Baylor College of Medicine receiving the highest number of citations among these high-output institutions (Table 2). The co-occurrence network of institutions within the field (Fig. 3C) can be divided into seven clusters. High-output institutions such as The University of Tokyo, Emory University, and Chiang Mai University serve as the core nodes of their respective clusters, possessing the highest number of co-occurrence connections within their clusters. In Fig. 3D, institutions with a greenish hue—represented by The University of Tokyo—have long been deeply engaged in the field of pediatric NoV infection and serve as the foundational forces supporting the field’s development; larger yellow nodes, such as Emory University, gained momentum rapidly during the middle and later stages of research, becoming the backbone of the field with the highest levels of research output and collaboration activity in recent years. Smaller bright yellow nodes, such as Chang Gung University and the Evandro Chagas Institute, represent emerging research forces that have gradually joined the global collaboration network in recent years. The overall institutional collaboration network has continued to expand over time, forming an evolutionary pattern characterized by the joint development of multiple tiers. Analysis of authors and cited authors A total of 1,049 researchers contributed to studies on NoV infection in children. The three most productive authors were Jan Vinje (81 publications), Hiroshi Ushijima (80), and Pattara Khamrin (59), with other highly productive authors mainly from Japan and the United States (Table 3). papers.title_zh: 过去28年全球儿童诺如病毒感染研究现状及关键问题的知识图谱映射与分析
papers.source_body_en: Therefore, this study employs bibliometric methods to conduct a visual analysis of the knowledge structure, research hotspots, and development trends in the global field of NoV infection research in children, providing a reference for future scientific research and the formulation of prevention and control strategies. Methods This study retrieved literature on pediatric NoV infections published between January 1998 and December 2025 from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) database. Using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and Bibliometrix software, we conducted a visual analysis of annual publication trends, countries/regions, institutions, authors, journals, keywords, and references to reveal the research trajectory, knowledge base, and cutting-edge directions in this field. Results This study included a total of 2,161 relevant publications. The results show that research on NoV infections in children worldwide has generally followed a steady upward trend, with activity remaining high in recent years. Conclusion Global research on NoV infections in children has evolved into a Multi-Disciplinary research framework driven by virology, epidemiology, clinical medicine, and public health. Abstract Background Norovirus (NoV) is a major pathogen responsible for acute gastroenteritis and outbreaks of diarrhea in humans. Children, due to their underdeveloped immune systems and higher risk of exposure, constitute a population with a relatively concentrated incidence of infection and disease burden. In recent years, research on NoV infections in children has been growing globally; however, there remains a lack of systematic quantitative analysis regarding the evolution of research themes, models of international collaboration, and future development directions in this field. papers.abstract_zh: 因此,本研究采用文献计量方法,对全球儿童诺如病毒感染研究领域的知识结构、研究热点和发展趋势进行可视化分析,为未来科学研究和防控策略的制定提供参考。方法 本研究从Web of Science核心合集(WoSCC)数据库中检索了1998年1月至2025年12月期间发表的关于儿童诺如病毒感染的文献。使用CiteSpace、VOSviewer和Bibliometrix软件,对年度发表趋势、国家/地区、机构、作者、期刊、关键词和参考文献进行了可视化分析,以揭示该领域的研究轨迹、知识基础和前沿方向。结果 本研究共纳入2,161篇相关文献。结果显示,全球儿童诺如病毒感染研究总体呈稳步上升趋势,近年来研究活动依然保持较高水平。结论 全球儿童诺如病毒感染研究已发展为由病毒学、诺如病毒、临床医学和公共卫生驱动的多学科研究框架。摘要 背景 诺如病毒(NoV)是人类急性胃肠炎和腹泻的主要病原体。由于儿童免疫系统尚未发育成熟且暴露风险较高,其感染和疾病负担相对集中。近年来,全球儿童诺如病毒感染研究不断增长;然而,该领域仍缺乏关于研究主题的系统定量分析、国际合作模式以及未来发展方向的深入探讨。该病毒具有高度传染性,传播迅速,全球广泛流行,被认为是全球疾病负担中导致失能调整生命年(DALYs)损失的第五大原因[1]。

papers.title: Enteric pathogens associated with diarrhea in children under five years of age in Yogyakarta, Indonesia (2017–2018): a hospital-based surveillance study
papers.abstract: Diarrhea is a major public health problem globally and remains an important cause of death and malnutrition in children under five years of age. In Indonesia, the burden of pediatric diarrhea remains substantial, yet most previous etiologic studies have focused on single pathogens, limiting understanding of the broader spectrum of enteric coinfections. This study aimed to identify the causes of diarrhea in hospitalized children under five years of age in Indonesia. Children aged < 5 years who were admitted to two participating hospitals in Yogyakarta with a diagnosis of diarrhea were prospectively recruited through active diarrhea surveillance between 2017 and 2018. Stool samples were collected during the first 48 h of admission and stored at -20 °C. Of 325 enrolled children, 171 stool samples (53%; 79 in 2017 and 92 in 2018) were randomly selected from eligible cases (acute, persistent, watery, or bloody diarrhea) by quarter, based on sufficient specimen availability. Multipathogen detection was performed using TaqMan Array Cards (TACs) at the Wellcome Trust Research Laboratory, Vellore, India. Targets with a cycle threshold (Ct) value < 40 were considered positive. Of the 325 hospitalized children, 171 (53%) underwent TAC testing (79 in 2017 and 92 in 2018). Rotavirus was the most frequently detected enteropathogen, accounting for 39% of TAC-tested samples in 2017 and 37% in 2018. Other commonly detected pathogens included adenovirus 40/41 (28% in 2017 and 3% in 2018), enteroaggregative Escherichia coli (EAEC) (27% and 28%, respectively), and norovirus GII (11% and 10%, respectively). The majority of rotavirus-positive samples had at least one additional pathogen detected (81% in 2017 and 74% in 2018), with bacterial pathogens being the most common coinfecting agents. Multiple pathogens detected in the same sample were recorded individually; however, co-infections were not analyzed as a separate category. Therefore, the potential contribution of co-infection to disease severity could not be fully assessed and should be considered a limitation of the study. Rotavirus remains the leading cause of hospitalization due to diarrhea in children under five years of age in Yogyakarta, Indonesia. These findings support continued monitoring of rotavirus vaccine impact and highlight the need for multi-pathogen surveillance to guide clinical management, antimicrobial stewardship, and immunization policy. Clinical trial number: not applicable.

analysis.methods: Stool samples were collected during the first 48 h of admission and stored at -20 °C. analysis.main_results: Norovirus GII.4 was detected in 10% of TAC-tested samples in 2018. Other commonly detected pathogens included adenovirus 40/41 (28% in 2017 and 3% in 2018), enteroaggregative Escherichia coli (EAEC) (27% and 28%, respectively), and norovirus GII (11% and 10%, respectively).

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support continued monitoring of rotavirus vaccine impact and emphasize the importance of understanding co-infections in pediatric diarrhea cases to improve clinical management and public health strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The potential contribution of co-infection to disease severity could not be fully assessed and should be considered a limitation of the study. analysis.summary_en: This study investigated enteric pathogens associated with diarrhea in children under five years of age in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, between 2017 and 2018. It aimed to identify the causes of diarrhea in hospitalized children and found that norovirus GII.4 was detected in 10% of TAC-tested samples in 2018. Other pathogens included adenovirus 40/41, enteroaggregative Escherichia coli, and norovirus GII. The study highlights the importance of multi-pathogen surveillance for better clinical management and public health strategies. However, it notes that co-infections were not analyzed as a separate category, which limits the assessment of their contribution to disease severity. The findings support continued monitoring of rotavirus vaccine impact and emphasize the need for understanding co-infections in pediatric diarrhea cases.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 腹泻是全球主要的公共卫生问题,仍然是5岁以下儿童死亡和营养不良的重要原因。本研究旨在确定印度尼西亚住院的5岁以下儿童腹泻的原因。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2017年至2018年间,通过主动腹泻监测,在日惹的两家参与医院中招募了年龄小于5岁的儿童,这些儿童被诊断为腹泻。在325名住院儿童中,171名(53%)接受了TAC检测(2017年79名,2018年92名)。
elements_zh.methods: 在入院后的前48小时内采集粪便样本,并在-20 °C下储存。使用印度维也纳信托研究实验室的TaqMan Array Cards(TACs)进行多病原体检测。循环阈值(Ct)值小于40的目标被视为阳性。
elements_zh.main_results: 在2018年的TAC检测样本中,检测到了10%的诺如病毒 GII.4。其他常见检测到的病原体包括腺病毒40/41(2017年28%,2018年3%)、肠聚集性大肠杆菌(EAEC)(27%和28%)以及诺如病毒 GII(11%和10%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究强调需要进行多病原体监测以指导临床管理、抗菌药物使用和疫苗接种政策。大多数轮状病毒阳性样本至少检测到一种其他病原体,其中细菌病原体是最常见的共感染病原体。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持继续监测轮状病毒疫苗的影响,并强调了解儿童腹泻病例中共感染的重要性,以改善临床管理和公共卫生策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 无法全面评估共感染对疾病严重程度的潜在贡献,这应被视为本研究的局限性。由于研究集中在特定地理区域且未将共感染作为独立类别进行分析,证据强度中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 腹泻是全球主要的公共卫生问题,仍然是5岁以下儿童死亡和营养不良的重要原因。在印度尼西亚,儿童腹泻的负担仍然显著,但大多数先前的病因研究都集中在单一病原体上,限制了对更广泛肠道共感染的理解。本研究旨在确定印度尼西亚日惹地区住院的5岁以下儿童腹泻的原因。2017年至2018年间,通过主动腹泻监测,在日惹的两家参与医院中招募了年龄小于5岁的儿童,这些儿童被诊断为腹泻。在入院后的前48小时内采集粪便样本,并在-20 °C下储存。在325名入选儿童中,根据样本充足性,按季度随机选取了171份粪便样本(53%;2017年79份,2018年92份)进行检测。使用印度维也纳信托研究实验室的TaqMan Array Cards(TACs)进行多病原体检测。循环阈值(Ct)值小于40的目标被视为阳性。在325名住院儿童中,171名(53%)接受了TAC检测(2017年79名,2018年92名)。轮状病毒是最常检测到的肠道病原体,占2017年TAC检测样本的39%和2018年的37%。其他常见检测到的病原体包括腺病毒40/41(2017年28%,2018年3%)、肠聚集性大肠杆菌(EAEC)(27%和28%)以及诺如病毒 GII(11%和10%)。大多数轮状病毒阳性样本至少检测到一种其他病原体(2017年81%,2018年74%),其中细菌病原体是最常见的共感染病原体。同一样本中检测到的多种病原体被单独记录,但共感染未被作为独立类别进行分析。因此,无法全面评估共感染对疾病严重程度的潜在影响,这应被视为本研究的局限性。轮状病毒仍然是印度尼西亚日惹地区5岁以下儿童因腹泻住院的主要原因。这些发现支持继续监测轮状病毒疫苗的影响,并强调需要进行多病原体监测以指导临床管理、抗菌药物使用和疫苗接种政策。临床试验编号:不适用。

papers.title: Pseudovirus Nanoparticles Displaying the Receptor-Binding Glycoprotein of Marburg Virus as Potential Vaccine Candidates
papers.abstract: Background: The lack of a licensed vaccine against the deadly Marburg virus (MARV) calls for the development of a novel and effective vaccine strategy. Methods: We report here our development of three pseudovirus nanoparticles (PVNPs), each displaying a MARV-neutralizing glycoprotein (GP) segment of different lengths, as MARV vaccine candidates. These PVNPs, designated S-GP278, S-GP377, and S-GP486, were generated using our proprietary norovirus shell nanoparticle (SNP) platform. The PVNPs were evaluated for their production, self-assembly, morphology, structural properties, and immunogenicity. Results: Our data demonstrated that the three recombinant S-GP proteins, S-GP278, S-GP377, and S-GP486, can be produced at low cost using an E. coli expression system. The purified recombinant S-GP proteins self-assembled into PVNPs with high efficacy. Structural modeling of the S-GP1 PVNPs highlighted their key architectural features, consisting of an icosahedral inner shell and multiple trimeric GP structures displayed on the surface. Immunization of mice with the S-GP PVNPs elicited high titers of GP-specific antibodies, including IgG and IgA. Conclusions: Collectively, these data support the notion that the S-GP PVNPs may serve as potential MARV vaccine candidates worthy of further development.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a novel vaccine strategy against the deadly Marburg virus (MARV) by creating pseudovirus nanoparticles (PVNPs) that display segments of the MARV-neutralizing glycoprotein (GP). The PVNPs, generated using a proprietary norovirus shell nanoparticle (SNP) platform, were evaluated for production, self-assembly, morphology, structural properties, and immunogenicity. The study provides a foundation for exploring new vaccine platforms against MARV, which could have significant implications for public health and the prevention of viral hemorrhagic fevers. However, the evidence does not report limitations or evidence strength for the study.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:缺乏针对致命马尔堡病毒(MARV)的获批疫苗,促使开发一种新型且有效的疫苗策略。方法:我们报告了三种假病毒纳米颗粒(PVNPs)的开发,每种PVNP展示不同长度的MARV中和糖蛋白(GP)片段,作为MARV 疫苗候选物。这些PVNPs,分别命名为S-GP278、S-GP377和S-GP486,是使用我们专有的诺如病毒壳纳米颗粒(SNP)平台生成的。对PVNPs进行了生产、自组装、形态、结构特性及免疫原性的评估。结果:我们的数据显示,三种重组S-GP蛋白S-GP278、S-GP377和S-GP486可通过大肠杆菌表达系统以低成本生产。纯化的重组S-GP蛋白能够高效自组装成PVNPs。S-GP1 PVNPs的结构建模突显了其关键的结构特征,包括一个二十面体的内壳和多个三聚体GP结构展示在表面。用S-GP PVNPs免疫小鼠可诱导产生高滴度的GP特异性抗体,包括IgG和IgA。结论:总体而言,这些数据支持S-GP PVNPs可能作为潜在的MARV 疫苗候选物,值得进一步开发。

papers.title: Deep untargeted wastewater metagenomic sequencing from sewersheds across the United States
papers.abstract: Wastewater monitoring enables non-invasive, population-scale tracking of community infections independent of healthcare-seeking behavior and clinical diagnosis. Metagenomic sequencing extends this capability by enabling broad, pathogen-agnostic detection of hundreds of viral taxa, including emerging threats. Here, we present data from CASPER (the Coalition for Agnostic Sequencing of Pathogens from Environmental Reservoirs), a U.S.-based wastewater metagenomic sequencing network designed for deep, untargeted pathogen monitoring at national scale. This release includes 1,206 samples collected between December 2023 and December 2025 from 27 sites across nine states, covering 13 million people. Deep sequencing (~1 billion read pairs per sample) generated 1.2 trillion read pairs (358 terabases), capturing diverse human, animal, and plant viruses including rare taxa. CASPER data tracks wastewater digital PCR and clinical abundance trends for SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, and respiratory syncytial virus, and recovers national-scale variant dynamics for SARS-CoV-2 and norovirus. As the largest publicly available untargeted wastewater sequencing dataset to date, CASPER provides a shared and growing resource for pathogen surveillance and microbial ecology.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to enhance the detection of human noroviruses through wastewater metagenomic sequencing, addressing the need for non-invasive, population-scale tracking of community infections that is independent of healthcare-seeking behavior and clinical diagnosis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved a U.S.-based wastewater metagenomic sequencing network called CASPER, which collected 1,206 samples between December 2023 and December 2025 from 27 sites across nine states, covering 13 million people.
analysis.methods: Deep sequencing (~1 billion read pairs per sample) was used to generate 1.2 trillion read pairs (358 terabases), capturing diverse human, animal, and plant viruses including rare taxa. CASPER data tracks wastewater digital PCR and clinical abundance trends for SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, and respiratory syncytial virus, and recovers national-scale variant dynamics for SARS-CoV-2 and norovirus.
analysis.main_results: The dataset includes comprehensive coverage of human noroviruses, with specific attention to Norovirus GI, Norovirus GII, and GII.4 norovirus, and provides insights into their variant dynamics at a national scale.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as demonstrating the potential of wastewater metagenomic sequencing for tracking norovirus variants and abundance trends, offering a novel approach for pathogen surveillance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform national-scale surveillance of norovirus infections and contribute to understanding the ecology and transmission dynamics of human noroviruses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on wastewater samples, which may not fully represent all population dynamics. However, as the largest publicly available untargeted wastewater sequencing dataset to date, it provides a robust resource for pathogen surveillance.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents the CASPER dataset, a large-scale wastewater metagenomic sequencing project designed to monitor human noroviruses across the United States. The research aimed to address the need for non-invasive, population-level tracking of community infections, independent of clinical diagnosis. Using deep sequencing, the study captured diverse viral taxa, including rare human norovirus variants, and provided insights into their abundance and dynamics. The findings highlight the potential of wastewater sequencing for surveillance and microbial ecology research, offering a novel approach for tracking norovirus infections. The dataset includes 1,206 samples from 27 sites across nine states, covering 13 million people, and is the largest publicly available untargeted wastewater sequencing resource. While the study is limited by its reliance on wastewater samples, it provides a valuable tool for understanding norovirus transmission and prevalence.

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其对废水样本的依赖而受到限制,该样本可能无法完全代表所有种群动态。然而,作为迄今为止最大的公开可用的非目标废水测序数据集,它为病原体 监测 提供了强大的资源。

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Tuesday, October 20, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Field investigation associates norovirus GII outbreak at Chinese university with canteen dining by October 20, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 Infected Canteen Workers Traced as Source of Norovirus GII.17 Outbreak at Chinese University Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A field investigation of an acute gastroenteritis outbreak at a university in Jinhua, China, identified 215 cases from December 14 to 24, 2024, with an overall attack rate of 0.48%. Most affected people experienced diarrhea and vomiting. The study authors reported that the epidemic curve was consistent with continuous exposure to a common source followed by secondary transmission, while laboratory testing found norovirus GII in 16 of 66 clinical, environmental and food-handler samples. Four positive samples were sequenced and identified as GII.17; genotypes for the other positive samples, including the sample described as the index case, were not available. The investigation combined a descriptive description of cases by time, symptoms and location with case–control and retrospective cohort studies examining dining exposures, hygiene behaviors and illness risk. The first-floor canteen in Zone A had the highest reported attack rate, at 1.14%, compared with 0.56% in Zone B and 0.42% in Zone C. The relative risk for Zone A versus Zone C was 2.71 (95% confidence interval, 1.89–3.89). Dining at the Zone A first-floor canteen was the primary food-related risk factor identified in the analysis, with an odds ratio of 18.85 (95% CI, 2.44–145.39). The reported association increased with the number of meals consumed: relative risks were 1.82 for two or three meals and 3.45 for more than three meals. Poor hand hygiene was also associated with illness, with an odds ratio of 14.60. Of the 66 tested samples, six positive samples came from canteen workers, including two from people without symptoms. Six infected workers continued working through December 20, and four were cashiers who handled takeaway packaging. Investigators also observed improper glove use and inadequate tableware disinfection in the canteen environment. The authors stated that the epidemiological pattern, together with the laboratory and environmental findings, strongly implicated foodborne transmission involving infected canteen staff, followed by person-to-person spread. The investigation did not establish a complete transmission chain, and the positive samples that were not sequenced could not be assigned a genotype. Discover more Research Assistant Listings iGEM Team Directory Bioengineering Events Calendar Bioengineer Blog Access Bioengineering Research Papers The study’s findings were based on the supplied published abstract and were reported in BMC Infectious Diseases as accepted research subject to further editing. Its scope was limited to one university outbreak and the available laboratory sequencing results. The investigators proposed staff health monitoring, standardized work practices, hand-hygiene promotion and prompt disinfection as components of outbreak control, but the abstract did not report a controlled evaluation of those measures or their effectiveness. analysis.location_and_population: The outbreak occurred at a university in Jinhua, China, affecting students and staff with an overall attack rate of 0.48%.
analysis.event: A field investigation identified a norovirus GII.17 outbreak at a Chinese university, associated with dining at the canteen, and reported by the study authors in BMC Infectious Diseases.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 215 cases were reported, with the first-floor canteen in Zone A having the highest attack rate (1.14%) and a relative risk of 2.71 compared to Zone C. Dining at Zone A canteen was the primary food-related risk factor with an odds ratio of 18.85. Poor hand hygiene was also associated with illness (odds ratio of 14.60).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The investigation combined case descriptions, case–control, and retrospective cohort studies. analysis.brief_en: A field investigation linked a norovirus GII.17 outbreak at a university in Jinhua, China, to dining at the canteen, with 215 cases reported from December 14 to 24, 2024. The attack rate was 0.48%, with the first-floor canteen in Zone A showing the highest rate at 1.14%. Laboratory testing identified norovirus GII in 16 of 66 samples, including six from canteen workers, two of whom were asymptomatic. The study found that dining at Zone A was the primary risk factor, with an odds ratio of 18.85, and that consuming more than three meals increased the relative risk. Poor hand hygiene was also associated with illness. While the investigation suggested foodborne transmission involving infected staff and subsequent person-to-person spread, it did not fully establish the transmission chain. The findings were reported in BMC Infectious Diseases and are subject to further editing. The study’s scope was limited to this university outbreak and available sequencing results, with proposed control measures including staff health monitoring, standardized work practices, and hand-hygiene promotion.

news.source_body_en: A field investigation linked a norovirus GII.17 outbreak at a university in Jinhua, China, to dining at the canteen, with 215 cases reported from December 14 to 24, 2024. The attack rate was 0.48%, with the first-floor canteen in Zone A showing the highest rate at 1.14%. Laboratory testing identified norovirus GII in 16 of 66 samples, including six from canteen workers, two of whom were asymptomatic. The study found that dining at Zone A was the primary risk factor, with an odds ratio of 18.85, and that consuming more than three meals increased the relative risk. Poor hand hygiene was also associated with illness. While the investigation suggested foodborne transmission involving infected staff and subsequent person-to-person spread, it did not fully establish the transmission chain. The findings were reported in BMC Infectious Diseases and are subject to further editing. The study’s scope was limited to this university outbreak and available sequencing results, with proposed control measures including staff health monitoring, standardized work practices, and hand-hygiene promotion.

news.content: By Jake Hardiman Published Oct 20, 2026, 6:43 AM EDT A graduate in German, Jake has a passion for history and regional aviation, and enjoys sampling new carriers and aircraft. He has visited OEM facilities as far and wide as Bristol, Toulouse, and Seattle, and recently enjoyed the milestone of flying his 150th sector as a passenger. Based in Norfolk, UK. Sign in to your Simple Flying account On Sunday evening, airport authorities at Germany's Düsseldorf Airport (DUS) prepared for a mass casualty event as a Eurowings Airbus A321-200 operating a flight from Rhodes (RHO) in Greece reported an illness outbreak onboard. Current suspicions suggest that it was an outbreak of norovirus, although this remains unconfirmed as Eurowings investigates the matter and those affected receive treatment. In any case, the scale of the outbreak ultimately proved to be lower than feared, with just a few of the plane's more than 200 passengers having to be taken to hospital. However, given the contagious nature of norovirus, the possibility of such an outbreak makes the scale of the response understandable. Despite its dramatic arrival in Düsseldorf , the plane was cleared to re-enter service the next day. Authorities Were Prepared For A Mass Casualty Event Credit: Simple Flying Eurowings flight EW9631 is a daily scheduled service that the German leisure carrier and Lufthansa Group subsidiary primarily operates in order to bring Düsseldorf-based holidaymakers back from Rhodes. According to Flightradar24, it is an evening service, with its departure penciled in for 7:20 PM on most days . Its arrival on Sunday, October 18, was set for 10:00 PM, with an A321 operating the flight. Quiz 3 Questions Flight Into Uncertainty Your Top Score -- Attempts -- Average 90% Users 58 Flight Into Uncertainty 0 0 Easy Question 1 of 3 Which Greek island was the departure point for Eurowings flight EW9631? Report Error Found an error? Send it info@simpleflying.com so it can be corrected. Sunday's iteration took off at 7:51 PM and landed at 10:03 PM, but the three-hour flight was not without drama. According to coverage of the matter by aero.de, Dusseldorf Airport triggered its mass casualty response alarm after reports emerged that passengers on the flight were experiencing severe discomfort . This resulted in multiple ambulances and fire engines being deployed, with Eurowings saying that: "The cause of the complaints is currently still unclear and is being investigated." The Flight Was Given Priority As It Came In To Land Credit: AlfonsoSM | Shutterstock A closer look at flight tracking data shows that Sunday's iteration of Eurowings flight EW9631 was faster than normal, with the service typically spending closer to three hours and 30 minutes in the air. However, with the service's crew having requested to be met by medical staff on arrival in Düsseldorf, the flight was given priority on its way in, resulting in its fastest airborne journey time in more than a week. The situation ultimately proved to be less of a mass casualty event than had initially been feared, with The Aviation Herald reporting that just three of the flight's passengers were taken to hospital . A grand total of 219 people were reported to have been on the flight: 212 guests and seven crew members. According to EuroNews, the cabin crew donned masks during the flight as fears of onboard contagion spread . EW9631 On October 18 Per Flightradar24 Departure Arrival Planned 7:20 PM 10:00 PM Actual 7:51 PM 10:03 PM The exact nature of the outbreak remains unconfirmed, but multiple reports highlight the fact that current suspicions are pointing towards norovirus. Elsewhere, theories of a gastrointestinal infection are also being considered. In any case, the situation was taken very seriously, with medical staff donning head-to-toe PPE and coming on board and questioning passengers about their symptoms after their arrival. The Aircraft Is Back In Service, Suggesting No Wider Concerns Credit: Markus Mainka | Shutterstock Due to this questioning, as well as other delays for which passengers were reportedly not told the reasoning, those on board the jet, a 14-year-old Airbus A321-200 that bears the registration D-AIDT, could not disembark until 11:30 PM, more than an hour after landing. This delay and lack of clarity are said to have led to further concerns and uncertainty among passengers who just wanted to get home. Either way, despite the potentially serious nature of the illness outbreak and the need for multiple passengers to be taken to hospital for further treatment and examination, it seems that the situation did not pose a wider concern for future occupants of the aircraft. It was back in the air the next day, operating a morning rotation to Mallorca (PMI) and back, before flying to Heraklion (HER) in the afternoon

news.content: Norovirus warning as cases above average – symptoms and how long to stay off work We haven't even entered winter yet, but cases of norovirus remain higher than average. Although activity of norovirus, also called the 'winter vomiting bug', has decreased in recent weeks, it remains higher than the 5-season average but within expected levels. The latest norovirus data published by the UK Health and Security Agency (UKHSA) on September 24 shows total norovirus laboratory reports between weeks 35 and 38 of 2026 were 36.9% higher than the 5-season average for the same 4-week period. Read more The 12 signs of COVID going around Birmingham right now – and when to stay home While cases tend to peak between November and April, especially as people start to spend more time indoors, there are symptoms you need to be aware of now. Norovirus often causes outbreaks because it is easily spread from one person to another and the virus is able to survive for many days in the environment. Symptoms start one to two days after you become infected and last for up to two or three days. It can be very unpleasant, but usually goes away in about two days. Norovirus symptoms The main symptoms of norovirus are: - feeling sick (nausea) - diarrhoea - being sick (vomiting) You may also have: - a high temperature of 38°C or above - a headache - aching arms and legs. Ensure our latest headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as your Preferred Source in your Google search settings. How long to stay off work The NHS stresses that people with norovirus should not go to work or school and should stay at home for at least 48 hours after diarrhoea and vomiting have completely stopped. It's also advised to stay away from care homes and hospitals while ill, and not to visit people with compromised immune systems. Read more Birmingham GP explains quick way to tell difference between a cold, flu and COVID How norovirus is spread You can catch norovirus from: - close contact with someone with norovirus - touching surfaces or objects that have been touched by someone with norovirus - eating food that has been prepared or handled by someone with norovirus What you can do to stop norovirus The most effective way to prevent the spread of norovirus is simply washing your hands regularly with soap and water. Remember that alcohol gels do not kill norovirus. Also avoid sharing cups, glasses and dishes and cutlery with others, or towels and flannels. Disinfect hard surfaces that an infected person has touched with a chlorine releasing agent, such as bleach. Always call 111 if your symptoms are severe for medical advice, or 999 if you need urgent medical help

supplementary_news.title: Field investigation associates norovirus GII outbreak at Chinese university with canteen dining
supplementary_news.excerpt: A field investigation of 215 gastroenteritis cases at a Chinese university associated the outbreak with dining at one canteen and found norovirus GII in 16 of 66 tested samples.
supplementary_news.rss_summary_html: A field investigation of 215 gastroenteritis cases at a Chinese university associated the outbreak with dining at one canteen and found norovirus GII in 16 of 66 tested samples.

supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Tuesday, October 20, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Field investigation associates norovirus GII outbreak at Chinese university with canteen dining by October 20, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 Infected Canteen Workers Traced as Source of Norovirus GII.17 Outbreak at Chinese University Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A field investigation of an acute gastroenteritis outbreak at a university in Jinhua, China, identified 215 cases from December 14 to 24, 2024, with an overall attack rate of 0.48%. Most affected people experienced diarrhea and vomiting. The study authors reported that the epidemic curve was consistent with continuous exposure to a common source followed by secondary transmission, while laboratory testing found norovirus GII in 16 of 66 clinical, environmental and food-handler samples. Four positive samples were sequenced and identified as GII.17; genotypes for the other positive samples, including the sample described as the index case, were not available. The investigation combined a descriptive description of cases by time, symptoms and location with case–control and retrospective cohort studies examining dining exposures, hygiene behaviors and illness risk. The first-floor canteen in Zone A had the highest reported attack rate, at 1.14%, compared with 0.56% in Zone B and 0.42% in Zone C. The relative risk for Zone A versus Zone C was 2.71 (95% confidence interval, 1.89–3.89). Dining at the Zone A first-floor canteen was the primary food-related risk factor identified in the analysis, with an odds ratio of 18.85 (95% CI, 2.44–145.39). The reported association increased with the number of meals consumed: relative risks were 1.82 for two or three meals and 3.45 for more than three meals. Poor hand hygiene was also associated with illness, with an odds ratio of 14.60. Of the 66 tested samples, six positive samples came from canteen workers, including two from people without symptoms. Six infected workers continued working through December 20, and four were cashiers who handled takeaway packaging. Investigators also observed improper glove use and inadequate tableware disinfection in the canteen environment. The authors stated that the epidemiological pattern, together with the laboratory and environmental findings, strongly implicated foodborne transmission involving infected canteen staff, followed by person-to-person spread. The investigation did not establish a complete transmission chain, and the positive samples that were not sequenced could not be assigned a genotype. The study’s findings were based on the supplied published abstract and were reported in BMC Infectious Diseases as accepted research subject to further editing. Its scope was limited to one university outbreak and the available laboratory sequencing results. The investigators proposed staff health monitoring, standardized work practices, hand-hygiene promotion and prompt disinfection as components of outbreak control, but the abstract did not report a controlled evaluation of those measures or their effectiveness.
